_law: HIS ORDERS, HELD BY THE MACHINE. Every row carries his words verbatim, the file those words still live in, what they command, where the repo obeys them, and — where it can be written as one — an ASSERTION against the actual code. The builder may not edit, soften, retire or out-argue a row here. He reverses his own orders, from the image, at any time, and that reversal is a decision row carrying new words and a later date.
_what_it_cost_to_learn: 2026-08-16, his count, not mine: he ordered the bed cloth ACQUIRED on 08-14 and again on 08-15 ("เอาผ้าที่ปั้นเองออก แล้วเอาโมเดลเตียงที่หามาใส่ให้ดู"). D-072, decided_by 'builder', put the hand-simulated cloth back as the default over one missing component, and the next round went on tuning its numbers. Ten decision rows in the register decide that one subject against an R8 stop-loss of two. Not one rung noticed, and the reason is exact: HIS WORDS WERE IN THE REGISTER THE WHOLE TIME, IN A FIELD NO CHECKER READS — D-052 and D-054 quote the order in `question` and leave `owner_override` null, so `decisions_check`'s lock (rule 4) never armed and the row stayed re-decidable by the builder who wrote it. build_room.py states it at its sharpest: line 1651 cites 'owner order 2026-08-14' and line 1668 read `_BED_CLOTH_ACQ = False`.
_the_trap_this_file_names: A CLASS order and an INSTANCE verdict are not the same object, and treating one as repealing the other is what happened on 2026-08-16. He ordered the CLASS acquired (08-14, 08-15). He then failed one INSTANCE by eye — "ผ้าบนเตียงยังเละอยู่เลย" about set 8635b5b9 — and the lane read that as permission to return to hand-simulating and spend the next round tuning its tone. The answer to 'this bought one is a mess' is A DIFFERENT PURCHASE. An instance verdict narrows what may ship; it never repeals the class.
_how_to_overrule: Say it while looking at a frame. The builder files a decision row with `decided_by: 'owner'`, your words in `owner_override`, and `override_date`; if it retires an order here, that order's `standing` goes false and `retired_by` names the row. Nothing in this file ever waits for you — R3 stands.
